source.title: On the training dynamics of deep networks with L2 regularization

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present. Some figure values are only shown graphically; no numerical values are inferred from those figures.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how explicit L2 regularization and training duration affect generalization and reports comparisons with zero regularization and different training setups. These are conceptual tests of explicit regularization and its conditions, rather than the original claim's random-label memorization or generalization-gap measurements.
record.gate_note: Reports test-accuracy sweeps and training curves under L2 and zero L2, including fixed versus scaled training budgets, learning-rate schedules, and limited-capacity examples. The main text also refers to additional setups in the supplement where the scaling does not hold. AUTOL2 comparisons are recorded where they compare its test accuracy with constant L2; they do not establish results about random-label memorization, optimizer rankings, or the other listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests how L2 strength and training duration affect peak test accuracy. None of V1–V8 names that comparison. It does not test random-label fitting, width-dependent generalization, architecture or optimizer rankings, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. In the tested overparameterized settings, sufficiently small positive L2 coefficients attain similar peak test accuracy when training time grows approximately as 1/λ; fixed budgets favor a nonzero coefficient. Small positive L2 can also outperform zero L2. The authors report exceptions and derive kernel decay for infinitely wide homogeneous networks under stated theoretical assumptions. AUTOL2 improves constant-learning-rate experiments but underperforms tuned constant L2 with the tested learning-rate schedule.
record.recipe_differences: Studies the effect of L2 coefficient and training duration on test accuracy, not random-label fitting or the original claim's listed comparisons. Uses SGD, momentum and a proposed dynamic L2 schedule across several architectures and datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with training budget (fixed versus proportional to 1/λ), learning-rate schedule, optimizer momentum, batch normalization, and whether the setup is in the overparameterized/large-width regime. AUTOL2 does not improve results with learning-rate schedules in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: In the studied overparameterized settings, time to peak test accuracy scales approximately as 1/λ, or 1/(ηλ) with vanilla SGD. Sufficiently small positive λ values reach similar peak accuracy when training duration scales accordingly; fixed budgets instead favor a nonzero λ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 strength controls the training time needed to reach peak generalization performance in some overparameterized networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The width-64 fully connected CIFAR-10 model peaks at nonzero λ even with extended training, and ResNet-50 on ImageNet does not recover small-λ performance by training longer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The inverse-L2 training-time scaling and small-L2 accuracy plateau depend on the model and training regime.

record.problems: Most experiments compare settings using one initialization (the authors state this in Supplementary A); exact accuracies for many sweeps are only plotted. The paper notes exceptions to its scaling behavior, and the ResNet-50/ImageNet results are harder for the authors to interpret because they use a learning-rate schedule. The AUTOL2 experiment with a learning-rate schedule was not hyperparameter tuned.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Several separate plotted values cannot be recovered from the text, so rows report the stated trends and cite the figures without inferring numerical values.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test-error changes from widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning and recovery conditions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their performance difference.
Dropout's effect, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as a correlate of generalization gaps and its ranking against alternative measures.
Accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not judgments that the reported L2 effects are unreadable or absent. Shared datasets, overparameterization, and longer-training interventions do not establish the comparisons required by those versions. The Discussion's statement that peak time is proportional to λ is a typographical inconsistency; the equations and results specify inverse proportionality.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior as width increases.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the effect of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD on held-out performance.
Large versus small batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including training-set-size and overfitting regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy versus L2 coefficient for fixed training time and training time proportional to λ⁻¹.

conditions.value: η starts at 0.2 and decays by factor 0.2 at 0.3T, 0.6T, 0.9T

rows.baseline: Fixed T=200 epochs; tuned constant λ=0.0005 gives test accuracy 0.967 in the prediction comparison
rows.value: With fixed T, performance degrades below an optimal λ; with T proportional to λ⁻¹, performance improves at smaller λ and approaches a constant for sufficiently small λ. At T=200, predicted λ≈0.0001 gives test accuracy 0.960 versus 0.967 at λ=0.0005.
rows.locator: Figure 1(a), section 2 learning-rate schedules; section 3 Optimal L2
rows.note: Numerical values for λ settings in Figure 1(a) are not stated in prose; the explicit 0.960 and 0.967 comparison appears in section 3.
rows.check: The fixed-versus-scaled training-budget result concerns L2, not batch size. Split off the 0.960 versus 0.967 comparison: it evaluates the authors' parameter-selection method against tuning and should not be a claim-evidence row.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AUTOL2 and compared with a tuned constant L2 setting.
rows.baseline: Tuned constant L2 parameter; exact value and numeric accuracy not stated in the main text
rows.value: AUTOL2 is reported to train significantly faster and achieve superior performance; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The reported comparison is the study's proposed L2 schedule against a tuned constant value.
rows.check: This evaluates the authors' AUTOL2 method against constant L2; it should not be a claim-evidence row.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared AUTOL2 against fixed L2 values in a learning-rate-schedule experiment.
rows.baseline: Fixed λ=0.0005 is stated to outperform AUTOL2 overall
rows.value: AUTOL2 trains faster in the beginning, but cannot keep pace with the constant-λ model's later jumps; numerical values are figure only.
rows.locator: Supplementary E, Figure S10; Figure S9 discussion
rows.note: The authors say they have not hyperparameter tuned possible AUTOL2 parameters; the fixed λ=0.0005 result is described as better in this setting.
rows.check: This evaluates AUTOL2 against constant L2 under a learning-rate schedule; it should not be a claim-evidence row. Its weaker performance does not constitute a partial effect for any listed version.

rows.subject: Fully connected network
rows.operation_detail: Varied L2 coefficient, learning rate and training duration in a setup that departs from the reported scaling behavior.
rows.measure: Maximum test accuracy and time to maximum test accuracy
rows.baseline: λ=0 comparison; exact accuracy values are figure only
rows.value: Unlike the main overparameterized setups, maximum test accuracy has a peak at some λopt≠0; time to peak scales like 1/λ for λ≳λopt but becomes constant at the λ=0 value for λ≲λopt; the peak occurs before training accuracy reaches 1.
rows.note: Authors attribute this departure to deviations from the overparameterized/large-width regime.
rows.check: This is a fixed-width L2 sweep, not a width sweep beyond interpolation or a controlled architecture comparison. Section D specifies three hidden layers.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate, weight decay and training schedule duration in an ImageNet experiment.
rows.baseline: λ or learning rate changed independently; exact reference values appear in figure only
rows.value: Performance for small λ did not improve even with longer training; performance was roughly constant along the η·λ diagonal. Exact values are figure only.
rows.note: Authors say they do not have as clear an understanding of these results because the experiment involves a learning-rate schedule, and attribute the difference to deviations from the overparameterized/large-width regime.
rows.check: Batch size stays fixed at 8192, so failure to recover accuracy by extending training does not test V5. Figure S8 provides numerical cell values, although the row records only the stated trend.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
